Marcus / Karthik —

Operational feasibility notes from infra review: we can provide a reservation certificate scoped to H100-compatible SKUs for the us-west-2 region for an initial 90-day window, with the following caveats:
- Certificate is a capacity assurance (reservation hold) tied to a named commitment and region — not a hard physical lock; in extreme cloud-level failures we will activate fallbacks (lower-latency cross-region options) with customer notification.
- We can support a one-time 14-day burst at up to 130% of baseline throughput if we reserve transient burst capacity. However, sustained burst at 120% permanently will require additional reserved units.
- KV-cache warming and pre-provisioning will require a 7-day lead time once the reservation is signed.

Commercial proposal (initial):
- Reservation: 90-day H100-family reservation hold; billable at committed rate, non-cancellable for 90 days.
- Burst: one one-time 14-day burst window; overage during the burst capped at $3.50/hr per H100 (this is a concession vs standard $5.00/hr).
- Post-burst: for the next 60 days we offer a smoothing overage cap of $4.25/hr to avoid sudden billing spikes.
- Onboarding credit: one-time 10% credit applied to first invoice or as a fixed $60k credit (whichever is greater).
- Early termination: waive ET surcharge for first 45 days (we still require 30-day notice after the 90-day period to unwind).

Attachments: I exported a short commercial summary (DLTA-Deal-Summary-terms.xlsx) and a draft MOU (mou-draft-Delta-20261121.docx) for legal to review.

If sales agrees to these numbers, we need formal exec approval for the H100 reservation hold and the temporary overage caps because the concession moves the deal economics materially. Karthik — can you model the P&L and margin impact by EOD? Aditya — please prepare a one-page MAP for Sam that calls out the 14-day burst activation criteria and the fallback plan.

- Laura
